activity_summary: Mistress Ansell boiled the oak-gall ink on the Monday copper from your receipt: galls, copperas and gum. The new horn was twopence on Saturday and is not paid again. Board, if you take it, is threepence, two or three times in a week. You left the fresh boil in the kitchen.

entities.name: William Shakespeare
entities.context: Named the receipt, and refused a second twopence.

entities.name: Mistress Dorcas Ansell
entities.context: Boiled it on the Monday copper, and restated the threepence.

entities.name: Alse Pinder
entities.context: Counted a hundred stirs, and left the new ink downstairs.

facets.activity: Stood out of the steam while the ink boiled

quotes.speaker: william_shakespeare
quotes.text: Galls, copperas, and gum. That is the receipt.

quotes.speaker: dorcas_ansell
quotes.text: Twopence the horn, and he had a new one on Saturday.

quotes.speaker: dorcas_ansell
quotes.text: If you board, it is threepence, and you do not board every night.
